---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m9p0t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Advisors, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES
    epoch,       \* current registration epoch (bumped on reconfiguration)
    st,          \* st[a]: "idle" | "waiting" | "using" the registration terminal
    net,         \* set of in-flight grant records; a bag reorderable in transit
    issued,      \* set of epochs for which a grant has already been dispatched
    curUser      \* the advisor the terminal currently believes is inside, or "none"

None == "none"
Grants == [to: Advisors, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ st \in [Advisors -> {"idle", "waiting", "using"}]
    /\ net \subseteq Grants
    /\ issued \subseteq (0..MaxEpoch)
    /\ curUser \in (Advisors \cup {None})

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ st = [a \in Advisors |-> "idle"]
    /\ net = {}
    /\ issued = {}
    /\ curUser = None

Submit(a) ==
    /\ st[a] = "idle"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![a] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, net, issued, curUser>>

\* Registrar dispatches at most one grant per epoch to a waiting advisor.
Issue(a) ==
    /\ st[a] = "waiting"
    /\ epoch \notin issued
    /\ net' = net \cup {[to |-> a, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ issued' = issued \cup {epoch}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, st, curUser>>

\* Reconfiguration only while nobody is inside; it opens a fresh epoch.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \A a \in Advisors : st[a] # "using"
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<st, net, issued, curUser>>

\* Entry is authorized by a grant that is still current (ep = epoch).
Enter(a) ==
    /\ st[a] = "waiting"
    /\ \E m \in net :
        /\ m.to = a
        /\ m.ep = epoch
        /\ net' = net \ {m}
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![a] = "using"]
    /\ curUser' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, issued>>

Exit(a) ==
    /\ st[a] = "using"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![a] = "idle"]
    /\ curUser' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, net, issued>>

\* A waiting advisor may give up before entering.
Abort(a) ==
    /\ st[a] = "waiting"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![a] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, net, issued, curUser>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : Submit(a)
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : Issue(a)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : Enter(a)
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : Exit(a)
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : Abort(a)

\* Mutual exclusion: whoever is inside the terminal is the one the registrar
\* records as the current user; two advisors cannot both be inside.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A a \in Advisors : st[a] = "using" => curUser = a

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Advisors = {a1, a2, a3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A university course-registration system exposes a single registration terminal
that advisors must use one at a time to commit a batch of enrollments. Access is
coordinated by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration scheme: the registrar keeps a
current epoch number, and periodically reconfigures the terminal (for example to
change section capacities), which advances the epoch. Each advisor first submits
a request and becomes waiting. The registrar dispatches at most one grant per
epoch to a waiting advisor; each grant is stamped with the epoch in effect when
it was sent. Because grant messages travel over a network that can reorder them,
a grant issued in an old epoch may still be sitting in transit after the registrar
has reconfigured. An advisor enters the terminal only when it holds a grant whose
stamped epoch equals the registrar's current epoch, at which point the registrar
records that advisor as the current user. Reconfiguration is permitted only while
no advisor is inside the terminal. When an advisor finishes it exits, clearing the
current-user record and returning to idle.

The action set is: Submit (an idle advisor becomes waiting), Issue (the registrar
dispatches one epoch-stamped grant per epoch to a waiting advisor), Reconfigure
(advance the epoch while nobody is inside), Enter (a waiting advisor holding a
current-epoch grant enters and is recorded as current user), Exit (a using advisor
leaves and clears the record), and Abort (a waiting advisor gives up and returns
to idle before entering).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any reachable state, any advisor recorded as inside the
registration terminal must be the single advisor the registrar currently records
as the terminal's user, so no two advisors ever occupy the terminal at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m4p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Robots, Schedulers, QCap

VARIABLES
    queue,     \* shared bounded intake queue of robots awaiting the charging bay
    pending,   \* pending[s]: robot scheduler s has pulled from the queue, or None
    owner,     \* the scheduler currently holding the single charging controller
    cs         \* cs[s]: TRUE while scheduler s is actively charging its robot

None == "none"

QHas(r) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = r
HeldSomewhere(r) == \E s \in Schedulers : pending[s] = r

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Robots)
    /\ Len(queue) <= QCap
    /\ pending \in [Schedulers -> Robots \cup {None}]
    /\ owner \in Schedulers \cup {None}
    /\ cs \in [Schedulers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ pending = [s \in Schedulers |-> None]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ cs = [s \in Schedulers |-> FALSE]

\* Backpressure: a robot may enter the intake queue only when it is below cap.
Arrive(r) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ ~QHas(r)
    /\ ~HeldSomewhere(r)
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, owner, cs>>

\* Either scheduler may pull the head of the shared queue when it has no robot.
Claim(s) ==
    /\ pending[s] = None
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = Head(queue)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, cs>>

\* Acquiring the charging controller is the critical section.
Enter(s) ==
    /\ pending[s] # None
    /\ ~cs[s]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = s
    /\ cs' = [cs EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, pending>>

Leave(s) ==
    /\ cs[s]
    /\ cs' = [cs EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Arrive(r)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Claim(s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Enter(s)
    \/ \E s \in Schedulers : Leave(s)

\* Mutual exclusion of the charging controller: any scheduler that is actively
\* charging must be the one recorded as holding the controller, so the two
\* independent schedulers can never both drive the single bay at once.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A s \in Schedulers : cs[s] => owner = s

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
    Schedulers = {s1, s2}
    QCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a single charging bay whose access is driven by a
charging controller. Two independent scheduler instances run against one shared
pool of robots and one shared intake queue. Robots arriving to charge are placed
on a bounded intake queue; the queue applies backpressure, refusing new arrivals
once it is at capacity. Either scheduler may pull the robot at the head of the
shared queue and hold it as its pending robot. To actually charge, a scheduler
must acquire the single charging controller, which is the critical resource: it
enters its critical section only when the controller has no owner, recording
itself as the owner and marking itself as actively charging. When a scheduler
finishes, it leaves the critical section, releases the controller, and clears its
pending robot.

The action set is: Arrive (a robot joins the bounded queue while below capacity),
Claim (a scheduler pulls the head robot from the shared queue into its pending
slot), Enter (a scheduler with a pending robot acquires the free controller and
begins charging), and Leave (a charging scheduler releases the controller and
clears its pending robot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any scheduler that is actively charging
a robot must be the scheduler recorded as owning the charging controller, so the
two independent schedulers can never both operate the single charging bay at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m0p3t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains

VARIABLES
    reqs,     \* set of in-flight allocation claims (train ids); the network reorders
    ackd,     \* ackd[t]: TRUE once the arbiter has read train t's claim (ready to CAS)
    owner,    \* the single train the junction slot is allocated to, or None
    inSlot    \* inSlot[t]: TRUE while train t believes it holds the junction slot

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ reqs \subseteq Trains
    /\ ackd \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ owner \in Trains \cup {None}
    /\ inSlot \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ ackd = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ inSlot = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

\* A train optimistically submits a claim; claims sit in a set the network may
\* deliver in any order.
Submit(t) ==
    /\ ~inSlot[t]
    /\ ~ackd[t]
    /\ t \notin reqs
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ackd, owner, inSlot>>

\* The arbiter reads a pending claim (no coordination with the current owner);
\* two claims can both be read while the slot still looks free.
Ack(t) ==
    /\ t \in reqs
    /\ ~ackd[t]
    /\ ackd' = [ackd EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, inSlot>>

\* Compare-and-set acquire: the read claim allocates the slot only if it is still
\* free at commit time. This guard is the sole exclusion mechanism.
Acquire(t) ==
    /\ ackd[t]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = t
    /\ inSlot' = [inSlot EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ ackd' = [ackd EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs>>

\* The compare failed (slot already taken); drop the read claim and retry later.
Retry(t) ==
    /\ ackd[t]
    /\ owner # None
    /\ ackd' = [ackd EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs, owner, inSlot>>

Release(t) ==
    /\ inSlot[t]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ inSlot' = [inSlot EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs, ackd>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Submit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Ack(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Acquire(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Retry(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Release(t)

\* No double allocation of the same slot: any train that believes it holds the
\* junction slot must be the single train the arbiter records as its owner, so the
\* slot is never allocated to two trains at once.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A t \in Trains : inSlot[t] => owner = t

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {t1, t2, t3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A subway signalling block system arbitrates a single critical junction slot that
at most one train may occupy at a time, using optimistic locking with retry. A
train that wants the junction optimistically submits an allocation claim; claims
accumulate in a pool that the signalling network may deliver in any order, so the
arbiter does not see them in submission order. The arbiter reads a pending claim
and marks that train as acknowledged, without coordinating against whoever might
currently hold the slot, so two claims can both be read while the slot still looks
free. An acknowledged train then attempts to acquire the slot with a
compare-and-set that succeeds only if the slot is still unowned at commit time; on
success the train is recorded as the slot's sole owner and believes it holds the
slot. If the compare fails because another train already owns the slot, the
acknowledged claim is dropped and the train retries later. The holder eventually
releases the slot, clearing the owner record.

The action set is: Submit (a train adds an optimistic claim to the reorderable
pool), Ack (the arbiter reads a pending claim and marks the train acknowledged),
Acquire (an acknowledged train compare-and-sets the free slot and becomes owner),
Retry (an acknowledged train whose compare fails drops its claim to retry), and
Release (the holder frees the slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any train that believes it holds the
junction slot must be the single train recorded as the slot's owner, so the
junction slot is never double-allocated to two different trains at once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m4p3t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Patrons, QCap

VARIABLES
    queue,      \* bounded reservation request queue (backpressure at QCap)
    prepared,   \* prepared[p]: TRUE once the desk has pulled p's request to serve
    owner,      \* the single patron the rare copy is allocated to, or None
    assigned    \* assigned[p]: TRUE while patron p believes the copy is theirs

None == "none"

InQueue(p) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i] = p

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Patrons)
    /\ Len(queue) <= QCap
    /\ prepared \in [Patrons -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ owner \in Patrons \cup {None}
    /\ assigned \in [Patrons -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ prepared = [p \in Patrons |-> FALSE]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ assigned = [p \in Patrons |-> FALSE]

\* Backpressure: a reservation joins the queue only while it is below capacity.
Request(p) ==
    /\ ~prepared[p]
    /\ ~assigned[p]
    /\ ~InQueue(p)
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, owner, assigned>>

\* The desk pulls the head reservation and prepares that patron. It does not check
\* the copy's current holder, so several patrons can be prepared at once.
Prepare(p) ==
    /\ queue # << >>
    /\ Head(queue) = p
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, assigned>>

\* Assigning the copy succeeds only if it is currently free; this is the one
\* guard that keeps the single copy from being double-allocated.
Assign(p) ==
    /\ prepared[p]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = p
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue>>

\* A prepared patron who finds the copy already out steps aside (no failure; a slow
\* patron is simply asked to try again) and clears its prepared mark.
StepAside(p) ==
    /\ prepared[p]
    /\ owner # None
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, owner, assigned>>

Return(p) ==
    /\ assigned[p]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, prepared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Request(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Prepare(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Assign(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : StepAside(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Return(p)

\* No double allocation of the same slot: any patron who believes the rare copy is
\* theirs must be the single patron the desk records as its owner, so the copy is
\* never allocated to two patrons at the same time.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A p \in Patrons : assigned[p] => owner = p

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Patrons = {p1, p2, p3}
    QCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A library book reservation system hands out a single rare copy of a title to at
most one patron at a time, coordinating requests through a bounded work queue with
backpressure. A patron requests the copy by joining a reservation queue; the queue
applies backpressure and refuses new reservations once it is at capacity. A service
desk pulls the reservation at the head of the queue and prepares that patron to be
served, without checking who currently holds the copy, so several patrons may be in
the prepared state at the same time. A prepared patron is assigned the copy only if
the copy is currently free; the assignment records that patron as the copy's sole
owner and the patron then believes the copy is theirs. Because patrons may be slow
but never fail, a prepared patron who finds the copy already checked out is never
dropped or timed out; it simply steps aside and clears its prepared mark, to try
again later. When a patron is finished it returns the copy, clearing the owner
record.

The action set is: Request (a patron joins the bounded reservation queue while it
is below capacity), Prepare (the desk pulls the head reservation and prepares that
patron), Assign (a prepared patron is given the copy only if it is free, becoming
its owner), StepAside (a prepared patron whose copy is already out clears its
prepared mark without failing), and Return (an owning patron returns the copy).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any patron who believes the rare copy is
theirs must be the single patron recorded as the copy's owner, so the copy is never
double-allocated to two different patrons at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m1p1t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, MaxVal

VARIABLES
    record,   \* the shared throughput-tally record all stations update
    applied,  \* count of update commits that have been performed
    token,    \* the ring token holder (only holder may touch the record), or None
    basis,    \* basis[s]: the record value station s last read as its update basis
    crashed   \* crashed[s]: TRUE if station s has silently stopped

None == "none"

Alive == {s \in Stations : ~crashed[s]}

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ applied \in 0..(2 * MaxVal)
    /\ token \in Stations \cup {None}
    /\ basis \in [Stations -> 0..MaxVal]
    /\ crashed \in [Stations -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ token = None
    /\ basis = [s \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = [s \in Stations |-> FALSE]

\* The ring hands the free token to an alive station.
Acquire(s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[s]
    /\ token = None
    /\ token' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, crashed>>

\* Releasing returns the token to the ring.
Release(s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[s]
    /\ token = s
    /\ token' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, crashed>>

\* The token holder reads the current record as the basis for its next update.
Read(s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[s]
    /\ token = s
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![s] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, token, crashed>>

\* A commit writes basis+1 into the record, but only if the basis is still current
\* (nothing has been written since the read). This freshness check is the sole
\* guard preventing a stale write from clobbering intervening updates.
Commit(s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[s]
    /\ token = s
    /\ basis[s] = record
    /\ record < MaxVal
    /\ record' = basis[s] + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, basis, crashed>>

\* A station may crash silently, but never the last alive one; the ring routes the
\* token past a crashed holder.
Crash(s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[s]
    /\ \E o \in Stations : o # s /\ ~crashed[o]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ token' = IF token = s THEN None ELSE token
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Acquire(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Release(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Read(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Commit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Crash(s)

\* No lost updates: the number of update commits performed equals the record's
\* value, so every committed update is reflected and none is silently clobbered by
\* a write based on a stale read.
NoLostUpdates ==
    record = applied

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxVal = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash stations that all update a single shared
throughput-tally record. Exclusive access to the record is granted by a token ring:
a circulating token is held by at most one station at a time, and only the token
holder may read or update the record. To make an update, the token holder first
reads the current record value as the basis for its update, then commits a new
value equal to that basis plus one. A commit is allowed only if the basis is still
current, that is, the record has not changed since the holder read it; this
freshness check is what prevents a station from writing a value computed from a
stale read and thereby clobbering updates made in between. One station on the line
may crash silently at any time, except that the last remaining alive station never
crashes; when the holder of the token crashes, the ring routes the token past it so
the line keeps running.

The action set is: Acquire (an alive station takes the free token), Release (the
holder returns the token to the ring), Read (the holder reads the record as its
update basis), Commit (the holder writes basis-plus-one, but only if the basis is
still current), and Crash (a station other than the last alive one stops silently,
dropping the token if it held it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of update commits performed
equals the value of the shared record, so no committed update is ever lost by being
overwritten with a value computed from a stale read.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m0p1t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Registrars, MaxSeats

VARIABLES
    enrolled,   \* the shared enrollment count for the section (the record)
    applied,    \* count of enrollment commits performed
    basis,      \* basis[r]: the enrollment value registrar r read as its basis
    hasRead,    \* hasRead[r]: TRUE while r holds a computed, uncommitted update
    capacity    \* the section capacity, which an administrator may change at runtime

TypeOK ==
    /\ enrolled \in 0..MaxSeats
    /\ applied \in 0..(2 * MaxSeats)
    /\ basis \in [Registrars -> 0..MaxSeats]
    /\ hasRead \in [Registrars -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxSeats

Init ==
    /\ enrolled = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ basis = [r \in Registrars |-> 0]
    /\ hasRead = [r \in Registrars |-> FALSE]
    /\ capacity = MaxSeats

\* Optimistic read: a registrar reads the current enrollment as its update basis.
Read(r) ==
    /\ ~hasRead[r]
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![r] = enrolled]
    /\ hasRead' = [hasRead EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, applied, capacity>>

\* Commit succeeds only if the enrollment still equals the read basis (no update
\* happened in between). That compare is the sole guard against a stale write that
\* would overwrite intervening enrollments.
Commit(r) ==
    /\ hasRead[r]
    /\ basis[r] = enrolled
    /\ enrolled < capacity
    /\ enrolled' = basis[r] + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ hasRead' = [hasRead EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<basis, capacity>>

\* The compare would fail (enrollment moved since the read); drop and retry.
StaleReset(r) ==
    /\ hasRead[r]
    /\ basis[r] # enrolled
    /\ hasRead' = [hasRead EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, applied, basis, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime.
SetCapacity(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, applied, basis, hasRead>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Read(r)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : Commit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Registrars : StaleReset(r)
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxSeats : SetCapacity(c)

\* No lost updates: the number of enrollment commits performed equals the shared
\* enrollment count, so no committed enrollment is ever lost by a stale-basis write.
NoLostUpdates ==
    enrolled = applied

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Registrars = {r1, r2, r3}
    MaxSeats = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A university course-registration system lets several registrars concurrently enroll
students into one section, all updating a single shared enrollment count. Updates
use optimistic locking with retry rather than a lock. To enroll a student, a
registrar first optimistically reads the current enrollment count as the basis for
its update. It then commits a new count equal to that basis plus one, but the commit
succeeds only if the enrollment count still equals the value it read, meaning no
other registrar has committed in the meantime; this compare is what stops a
registrar from writing a count computed from a stale read and thereby losing
enrollments that happened in between. If the compare would fail because the count
moved, the registrar drops its pending update and retries with a fresh read. The
section capacity may be changed at runtime by an administrator, and a commit is only
permitted while the enrollment is below the current capacity.

The action set is: Read (a registrar optimistically reads the enrollment as its
update basis), Commit (a registrar writes basis-plus-one, but only if the count is
unchanged and below capacity), StaleReset (a registrar whose basis is stale drops
its pending update to retry), and SetCapacity (an administrator changes the section
capacity at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of enrollment commits performed
equals the shared enrollment count, so no committed enrollment is ever lost by being
overwritten with a count computed from a stale read.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m8p0t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, CoarseLocks

VARIABLES
    coarse,      \* coarse[cl]: the train holding coarse region lock cl, or None
    heldCoarse,  \* heldCoarse[t]: the coarse lock train t currently holds, or None
    wantsFine,   \* wantsFine[t]: TRUE once t (holding a coarse lock) wants the crossing
    crossing,    \* the fine lock: the single train granted the shared crossing, or None
    inCS         \* inCS[t]: TRUE while train t is inside the crossing critical section

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [CoarseLocks -> Trains \cup {None}]
    /\ heldCoarse \in [Trains -> CoarseLocks \cup {None}]
    /\ wantsFine \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ crossing \in Trains \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [cl \in CoarseLocks |-> None]
    /\ heldCoarse = [t \in Trains |-> None]
    /\ wantsFine = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]
    /\ crossing = None
    /\ inCS = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

\* Level one: a train takes a free coarse region lock. Different trains can hold
\* different coarse locks concurrently.
GrabCoarse(t, cl) ==
    /\ heldCoarse[t] = None
    /\ ~inCS[t]
    /\ coarse[cl] = None
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![cl] = t]
    /\ heldCoarse' = [heldCoarse EXCEPT ![t] = cl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wantsFine, crossing, inCS>>

\* Holding its coarse lock, a train declares intent for the fine crossing lock.
\* This does not consult the crossing, so several trains can want it at once.
ReadyFine(t) ==
    /\ heldCoarse[t] # None
    /\ ~wantsFine[t]
    /\ ~inCS[t]
    /\ wantsFine' = [wantsFine EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse, crossing, inCS>>

\* Level two: the fine crossing lock is granted only if it is free. This is the
\* sole guard enforcing mutual exclusion of the crossing.
GrabFine(t) ==
    /\ wantsFine[t]
    /\ crossing = None
    /\ crossing' = t
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ wantsFine' = [wantsFine EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse>>

ReleaseFine(t) ==
    /\ inCS[t]
    /\ crossing' = None
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse, wantsFine>>

ReleaseCoarse(t) ==
    /\ heldCoarse[t] # None
    /\ ~inCS[t]
    /\ ~wantsFine[t]
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![heldCoarse[t]] = None]
    /\ heldCoarse' = [heldCoarse EXCEPT ![t] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wantsFine, crossing, inCS>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, cl \in CoarseLocks : GrabCoarse(t, cl)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : ReadyFine(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : GrabFine(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : ReleaseFine(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : ReleaseCoarse(t)

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any train inside the crossing must be
\* the single train the fine lock records as holder, so two trains never occupy the
\* shared crossing at the same time even though a slow train may dwell there.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A t \in Trains : inCS[t] => crossing = t

nl:
A subway signalling block system protects a single shared crossing using
hierarchical locks acquired coarse-first then fine. There are several coarse region
locks and one fine crossing lock. To pass through the shared crossing, a train must
first take a free coarse region lock; different trains can hold different coarse
locks at the same time. Holding its coarse lock, a train then declares that it wants
the fine crossing lock, without consulting who currently holds the crossing, so
several trains can be waiting for the crossing simultaneously. The fine crossing
lock is granted to a train only if the crossing is currently free, and that grant is
the sole mechanism enforcing exclusive occupancy of the crossing. A train inside the
crossing eventually releases the fine lock, and a train not using or waiting for the
crossing may release its coarse lock. A train may be slow but never fails, so a slow
train that has grabbed the crossing is never evicted; it simply holds it until it
releases, and the crossing stays exclusive throughout.

The action set is: GrabCoarse (a train takes a free coarse region lock), ReadyFine
(a coarse-lock holder declares intent for the crossing without checking it), GrabFine
(the crossing lock is granted only if the crossing is free), ReleaseFine (a train in
the crossing releases the fine lock), and ReleaseCoarse (an idle train releases its
coarse lock).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any train inside the crossing must be the
single train recorded as holding the fine crossing lock, so two trains never occupy
the shared crossing at the same time.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m5p3t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Dispensers, Voters, Quorum, MaxDisp

VARIABLES
    votes,      \* votes[d]: set of voters that have voted for dispenser d this round
    owner,      \* the dispenser instance the single dose slot is allocated to, or None
    allocated,  \* allocated[d]: TRUE while instance d believes it holds the slot
    dispensed   \* count of completed dispenses (bounded activity counter)

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ votes \in [Dispensers -> SUBSET Voters]
    /\ owner \in Dispensers \cup {None}
    /\ allocated \in [Dispensers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ dispensed \in 0..MaxDisp

Init ==
    /\ votes = [d \in Dispensers |-> {}]
    /\ owner = None
    /\ allocated = [d \in Dispensers |-> FALSE]
    /\ dispensed = 0

\* A voter approves one dispenser's claim, but only if it has not already voted for
\* any dispenser this round. This single-vote rule is the sole guard that keeps two
\* instances from each gathering a quorum for the same slot.
Vote(d, v) ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ ~allocated[d]
    /\ \A dd \in Dispensers : v \notin votes[dd]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, allocated, dispensed>>

\* A voter may retract its vote before any allocation completes.
Withdraw(d, v) ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ ~allocated[d]
    /\ v \in votes[d]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![d] = votes[d] \ {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, allocated, dispensed>>

\* Once a dispenser has a quorum it allocates the slot. There is no separate lock on
\* the slot; exclusivity relies entirely on quorums being unable to overlap.
Allocate(d) ==
    /\ Cardinality(votes[d]) >= Quorum
    /\ ~allocated[d]
    /\ owner' = d
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dispensed>>

Release(d) ==
    /\ allocated[d]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ votes' = [dd \in Dispensers |-> {}]
    /\ dispensed' = IF dispensed < MaxDisp THEN dispensed + 1 ELSE dispensed

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, v \in Voters : Vote(d, v)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers, v \in Voters : Withdraw(d, v)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Allocate(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispensers : Release(d)

\* No double allocation of the same slot: any instance that believes it holds the
\* dose slot must be the single instance recorded as its owner, so the two
\* independent dispenser instances never both allocate the same slot.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A d \in Dispensers : allocated[d] => owner = d

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Dispensers = {d1, d2}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxDisp = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser runs two independent dispenser instances that
share one pool of dose slots. To allocate a dose slot, an instance must win a quorum
of approving votes rather than take a lock. Each round, voters approve claims: a
voter may approve at most one dispenser instance for the slot, and this single-vote
rule is the only thing that keeps the two instances from each assembling a quorum for
the same slot. A voter may retract its vote before any allocation has completed. Once
an instance has gathered a quorum of votes it allocates the dose slot and records
itself as the slot's owner; there is no separate lock guarding the slot, so
correctness depends entirely on two quorums being unable to overlap. When an instance
finishes dispensing it releases the slot, clears the owner record, resets the votes
for a fresh round, and advances the dispense counter.

The action set is: Vote (a voter approves one instance's claim, only if it has not
voted this round), Withdraw (a voter retracts its vote before any allocation), Allocate
(an instance with a quorum takes the slot and becomes owner), and Release (the owning
instance finishes, freeing the slot and resetting the round).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any dispenser instance that believes it
holds the dose slot must be the single instance recorded as the slot's owner, so the
same dose slot is never double-allocated to both instances at once.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m8p1t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, MaxVal

VARIABLES
    balance,     \* the shared settlement-batch record value
    applied,     \* count of settlement commits performed
    lockCoarse,  \* holder of the coarse account-group lock, or None
    lockFine,    \* holder of the fine account lock (taken only after coarse), or None
    msgs         \* set of in-flight commit messages [bank, base]; the network reorders

None == "none"

PendingFrom(b) == \E m \in msgs : m.bank = b

TypeOK ==
    /\ balance \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ applied \in 0..(2 * MaxVal)
    /\ lockCoarse \in Banks \cup {None}
    /\ lockFine \in Banks \cup {None}
    /\ msgs \subseteq [bank : Banks, base : 0..MaxVal]

Init ==
    /\ balance = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ lockCoarse = None
    /\ lockFine = None
    /\ msgs = {}

\* Level one: take the free coarse account-group lock.
GrabCoarse(b) ==
    /\ lockCoarse = None
    /\ ~PendingFrom(b)
    /\ lockCoarse' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, applied, lockFine, msgs>>

\* Level two: take the fine account lock, but only while holding the coarse lock.
GrabFine(b) ==
    /\ lockCoarse = b
    /\ lockFine = None
    /\ lockFine' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, applied, lockCoarse, msgs>>

\* Read the current balance as the update basis and emit a commit message, then
\* release both locks. Because the locks are freed before the message is applied,
\* two messages carrying the same basis can be in flight at once.
SubmitCommit(b) ==
    /\ lockFine = b
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[bank |-> b, base |-> balance]}
    /\ lockFine' = None
    /\ lockCoarse' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, applied>>

\* Apply a commit only if its basis still matches the balance. This freshness check
\* is the sole guard against a reordered stale message losing intervening updates.
ApplyCommit(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ m.base = balance
    /\ balance < MaxVal
    /\ balance' = m.base + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockCoarse, lockFine>>

\* A message whose basis is stale is discarded.
Drop(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ m.base # balance
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, applied, lockCoarse, lockFine>>

\* When the batch fills up it closes and a fresh batch opens; the record and the
\* commit count reset together so no committed settlement is left unaccounted.
Close ==
    /\ balance = MaxVal
    /\ balance' = 0
    /\ applied' = 0
    /\ msgs' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockCoarse, lockFine>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : GrabCoarse(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : GrabFine(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : SubmitCommit(b)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : ApplyCommit(m)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : Drop(m)
    \/ Close

\* No lost updates: the number of settlement commits performed equals the shared
\* balance record, so no committed settlement is ever lost by a reordered stale write.
NoLostUpdates ==
    balance = applied

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
    MaxVal = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is updated by several banks against one shared
settlement record. Access is arbitrated with hierarchical locks taken coarse-first
then fine: a bank must first take the coarse account-group lock, and only then may it
take the fine account lock. Holding the fine lock, a bank reads the current balance as
the basis for its update, emits a commit message carrying that basis, and immediately
releases both locks. Commit messages travel over a network that can reorder them, and
because the locks are released before a message is applied, two messages carrying the
same basis can be in flight at the same time. A commit message is applied only if its
basis still matches the current balance, meaning nothing has been applied since it was
read; this freshness check is the sole guard that stops a reordered, stale message from
overwriting settlements that were applied in between. A message whose basis is stale is
simply discarded.

The action set is: GrabCoarse (take the free coarse account-group lock), GrabFine
(take the fine account lock while holding the coarse lock), SubmitCommit (read the
balance as basis, emit a commit message, and release both locks), ApplyCommit (apply a
message only if its basis still matches the balance, advancing the record), Drop
(discard a message whose basis is stale), and Close (when the batch is full, reset the
record and the commit count together to open a fresh batch).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of settlement commits performed
equals the shared balance record, so no committed settlement is ever lost by being
overwritten with a value computed from a stale, reordered read.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m7p0t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxShed

VARIABLES
    reg,      \* the compare-and-swap register: id of the master-relay holder, or None
    wants,    \* wants[i]: TRUE once instance i intends to seize the relay
    inCS,     \* inCS[i]: TRUE while instance i is operating the master relay
    shed      \* count of load-shed operations drawn from the shared pool

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Instances \cup {None}
    /\ wants \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ inCS \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ shed \in 0..MaxShed

Init ==
    /\ reg = None
    /\ wants = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ inCS = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ shed = 0

\* An instance declares intent to seize the relay, without consulting the register,
\* so both instances can be contending at once.
Request(i) ==
    /\ ~wants[i]
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, shed>>

\* Compare-and-swap the register from None to this instance: succeeds only when the
\* register is empty. This swap is the sole guard enforcing mutual exclusion.
CASAcquire(i) ==
    /\ wants[i]
    /\ reg = None
    /\ reg' = i
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shed>>

\* The swap failed (register already taken); drop intent and retry later.
CASFail(i) ==
    /\ wants[i]
    /\ reg # None
    /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, shed>>

\* The relay holder performs a shed operation on the shared pool.
Shed(i) ==
    /\ inCS[i]
    /\ shed < MaxShed
    /\ shed' = shed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, wants, inCS>>

\* Compare-and-swap the register back to None on the way out.
CASRelease(i) ==
    /\ inCS[i]
    /\ reg' = None
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wants, shed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Request(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CASAcquire(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CASFail(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Shed(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CASRelease(i)

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any instance operating the master relay
\* must be the single instance the register records as holder, so the two independent
\* load-shedder instances never operate the shared relay at the same time.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A i \in Instances : inCS[i] => reg = i

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Instances = {g1, g2}
    MaxShed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A power-grid load shedder runs two independent controller instances that share one
pool of shed operations, coordinated through a single compare-and-swap register that
names the holder of the master relay. To operate the shared master relay, an instance
first declares its intent to seize it, without consulting the register, so both
instances can be contending at the same time. It then attempts a compare-and-swap that
sets the register from empty to its own id; the swap succeeds only if the register is
currently empty, and this swap is the sole mechanism enforcing exclusive use of the
relay. If the swap fails because the register is already taken, the instance drops its
intent and retries later. While it holds the relay, an instance performs shed
operations drawn from the shared pool. On the way out it compare-and-swaps the register
back to empty.

The action set is: Request (an instance declares intent without consulting the register),
CASAcquire (an instance swaps the empty register to its id, taking the relay), CASFail
(an instance whose swap fails drops its intent to retry), Shed (the relay holder performs
a shed operation from the shared pool), and CASRelease (the holder swaps the register back
to empty).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any instance operating the master relay must be
the single instance the compare-and-swap register records as its holder, so the two
independent load-shedder instances never operate the shared relay at the same time.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m6p6t3 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, MaxServed

VARIABLES
    valid,    \* valid[p]: TRUE while participant p holds a currently valid lease
    holder,   \* the participant the lease is currently granted to, or None
    acting,   \* acting[p]: TRUE while p is performing the protected shed action
    served    \* count of completed protected actions (bounded activity counter)

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ valid \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ holder \in Participants \cup {None}
    /\ acting \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ served \in 0..MaxServed

Init ==
    /\ valid = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
    /\ holder = None
    /\ acting = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
    /\ served = 0

\* Grant a fresh, valid lease to a participant when none is held.
Grant(p) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ ~valid[p]
    /\ holder' = p
    /\ valid' = [valid EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, served>>

\* A new grant preempts a slow (but not failed) holder that is not mid-action,
\* invalidating its lease; the preempted holder becomes stale.
Preempt(p, q) ==
    /\ holder = p
    /\ p # q
    /\ ~acting[p]
    /\ holder' = q
    /\ valid' = [valid EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE, ![q] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, served>>

\* The lease simply expires for an idle holder, leaving it stale.
Expire(p) ==
    /\ holder = p
    /\ ~acting[p]
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ valid' = [valid EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, served>>

\* The protected action is permitted only while the participant's lease is valid;
\* this validity check is the sole guard against a stale participant acting.
Act(p) ==
    /\ valid[p]
    /\ ~acting[p]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<valid, holder, served>>

Finish(p) ==
    /\ acting[p]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ served' = IF served < MaxServed THEN served + 1 ELSE served
    /\ UNCHANGED <<valid, holder>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Grant(p)
    \/ \E p, q \in Participants : Preempt(p, q)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Expire(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Act(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : Finish(p)

\* No action by an unauthorized or stale participant: any participant performing the
\* protected action must currently hold a valid lease, so a participant whose lease
\* has expired or been preempted can never act.
NoStaleAction ==
    \A p \in Participants : acting[p] => valid[p]

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
    MaxServed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A power-grid load shedder grants the right to perform a protected shedding action
using lease-based ownership with expiry. At most one participant holds a valid lease
at a time. A lease is granted to a participant when none is currently held. A newer
grant may preempt a slow but not failed holder that is not currently mid-action,
invalidating the old holder's lease so that it becomes stale; likewise an idle
holder's lease may simply expire, leaving it stale. Because participants are slow but
never fail, a preemption or expiry is only allowed while the holder is not in the
middle of its action, so a slow holder finishing an action is never cut off. The
protected shedding action is permitted only while the acting participant's lease is
still valid, and this validity check is the sole guard that stops a stale participant
whose lease has expired or been preempted from acting.

The action set is: Grant (give a fresh valid lease when none is held), Preempt (a new
grant takes the lease from a slow, non-acting holder, invalidating it), Expire (an
idle holder's lease expires and is invalidated), Act (a participant begins the
protected action only if its lease is valid), and Finish (an acting participant
completes its action).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any participant performing the protected
shedding action must currently hold a valid lease, so a participant whose lease has
expired or been preempted can never perform the action.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m8p0t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Members, CoarseLocks

VARIABLES
    coarse,       \* coarse[cl]: the member holding coarse book-section lock cl, or None
    heldCoarse,   \* heldCoarse[m]: the coarse lock member m holds, or None
    wantsEngine,  \* wantsEngine[m]: TRUE once m (holding a coarse lock) wants the engine
    engine,       \* the fine lock: the single member granted the match engine, or None
    inCS,         \* inCS[m]: TRUE while member m is crossing on the match engine
    crashed       \* crashed[m]: TRUE if member m has silently crashed

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [CoarseLocks -> Members \cup {None}]
    /\ heldCoarse \in [Members -> CoarseLocks \cup {None}]
    /\ wantsEngine \in [Members -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ engine \in Members \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Members -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ crashed \in [Members -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [cl \in CoarseLocks |-> None]
    /\ heldCoarse = [m \in Members |-> None]
    /\ wantsEngine = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ engine = None
    /\ inCS = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]
    /\ crashed = [m \in Members |-> FALSE]

\* Level one: take a free coarse order-book-section lock.
GrabCoarse(m, cl) ==
    /\ ~crashed[m]
    /\ heldCoarse[m] = None
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ coarse[cl] = None
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![cl] = m]
    /\ heldCoarse' = [heldCoarse EXCEPT ![m] = cl]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wantsEngine, engine, inCS, crashed>>

\* Declare intent for the fine match-engine lock, without consulting the engine, so
\* members holding different coarse locks can want it at once.
ReadyEngine(m) ==
    /\ ~crashed[m]
    /\ heldCoarse[m] # None
    /\ ~wantsEngine[m]
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ wantsEngine' = [wantsEngine EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse, engine, inCS, crashed>>

\* Level two: the match engine is granted only if it is free. Sole exclusion guard.
GrabEngine(m) ==
    /\ ~crashed[m]
    /\ wantsEngine[m]
    /\ engine = None
    /\ engine' = m
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ wantsEngine' = [wantsEngine EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse, crashed>>

ReleaseEngine(m) ==
    /\ inCS[m]
    /\ engine' = None
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, heldCoarse, wantsEngine, crashed>>

ReleaseCoarse(m) ==
    /\ heldCoarse[m] # None
    /\ ~inCS[m]
    /\ ~wantsEngine[m]
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![heldCoarse[m]] = None]
    /\ heldCoarse' = [heldCoarse EXCEPT ![m] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wantsEngine, engine, inCS, crashed>>

\* A member may crash silently (never the last alive one); the exchange reclaims any
\* locks it held, including the match engine, so the auction keeps running.
Crash(m) ==
    /\ ~crashed[m]
    /\ \E o \in Members : o # m /\ ~crashed[o]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ wantsEngine' = [wantsEngine EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ engine' = IF engine = m THEN None ELSE engine
    /\ coarse' = [cl \in CoarseLocks |-> IF coarse[cl] = m THEN None ELSE coarse[cl]]
    /\ heldCoarse' = [heldCoarse EXCEPT ![m] = None]

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, cl \in CoarseLocks : GrabCoarse(m, cl)
    \/ \E m \in Members : ReadyEngine(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : GrabEngine(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : ReleaseEngine(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : ReleaseCoarse(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members : Crash(m)

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any member crossing on the match engine
\* must be the single member the fine lock records as holder, so two members never
\* cross on the shared engine at once, even as members crash silently.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A m \in Members : inCS[m] => engine = m

=============================================================================
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction crosses orders on a single shared match engine that
only one member may drive at a time, using hierarchical locks taken coarse-first then
fine. There are several coarse order-book-section locks and one fine match-engine lock.
To cross, a member must first take a free coarse section lock; different members can
hold different coarse locks at the same time. Holding its coarse lock, a member then
declares that it wants the fine match-engine lock, without consulting who currently
holds the engine, so several members can be waiting for the engine at once. The engine
lock is granted to a member only if the engine is currently free, and that grant is the
sole mechanism enforcing exclusive use of the engine. A member on the engine eventually
releases it, and an idle member may release its coarse lock. Any member except the last
alive one may crash silently; when it does, the exchange reclaims every lock it held,
including the match engine, so the auction keeps running.

The action set is: GrabCoarse (take a free coarse section lock), ReadyEngine (a coarse
holder declares intent for the engine without checking it), GrabEngine (the engine is
granted only if it is free), ReleaseEngine (a crossing member releases the engine),
ReleaseCoarse (an idle member releases its coarse lock), and Crash (a member other than
the last alive one crashes silently, its locks reclaimed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any member crossing on the match engine must
be the single member recorded as holding the fine match-engine lock, so two members
never drive the shared engine at the same time.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m3p2t3 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, Total, MaxTerm

VARIABLES
    tok,      \* tok[l]: access credentials currently homed at door lock l
    transit,  \* credentials picked up by the leader and in transit between locks
    leader,   \* the elected coordinator lock, or None
    term      \* the current election term (advanced on failover)

None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumF(_)
SumF(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN tok[x] + SumF(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ tok \in [Locks -> 0..Total]
    /\ transit \in 0..Total
    /\ leader \in Locks \cup {None}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm

Init ==
    /\ tok = [l \in Locks |-> IF l = CHOOSE z \in Locks : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ leader = None
    /\ term = 0

\* Leader election: with no leader, a lock is elected and the term advances.
Elect(l) ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ leader' = l
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, transit>>

\* Failover: a slow but not failed leader is timed out, prompting re-election. Any
\* credentials it had in transit are not lost.
Timeout ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, transit, term>>

\* The leader lifts one credential off a lock into transit.
SendCredential(from) ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ tok[from] > 0
    /\ transit < Total
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![from] = tok[from] - 1]
    /\ transit' = transit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

\* The leader sets an in-transit credential down onto a lock.
DeliverCredential(to) ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ transit > 0
    /\ tok[to] < Total
    /\ transit' = transit - 1
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![to] = tok[to] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Elect(l)
    \/ Timeout
    \/ \E from \in Locks : SendCredential(from)
    \/ \E to \in Locks : DeliverCredential(to)

\* Conservation of a quantity: the credentials homed on locks plus those in transit
\* always sum to the fixed total, so no access credential is ever created or destroyed
\* by the network, even across leader failover.
Conservation ==
    SumF(Locks) + transit = Total

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Locks = {l1, l2, l3}
    Total = 2
    MaxTerm = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A smart-home door lock network shares a fixed pool of access credentials distributed
across its door locks, coordinated by a leader elected with failover. The total number
of credentials in the whole network is fixed. When there is no leader, a lock is
elected as coordinator and the election term advances. A slow but not failed leader may
be timed out, prompting a re-election; any credential the leader is carrying stays in
transit and is not lost across the failover. Under a leader, credentials are re-homed
one at a time: the leader lifts a credential off one lock into transit, and later sets
an in-transit credential down onto another lock. A credential is therefore always
either homed on exactly one lock or in transit, and the network never mints a new
credential or discards one.

The action set is: Elect (with no leader, elect a coordinator lock and advance the
term), Timeout (drop a slow leader to prompt failover, keeping any in-transit
credential), SendCredential (the leader lifts one credential off a lock into transit),
and DeliverCredential (the leader sets an in-transit credential down onto a lock).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the credentials homed on locks plus those in
transit sum to exactly the fixed total, so no access credential is ever created or
destroyed by the network.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m8p4t5 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Cap, MaxOverride, MaxWashed

VARIABLES
    status,    \* status[c]: "out" | "atGate" | "ready" | "online"
    gate,      \* the coarse entry-gate lock holder (a car passing the gate), or None
    override,  \* remaining privileged admin overrides
    washed     \* count of cars that have finished and left the conveyor

None == "none"

Online == {c \in Cars : status[c] = "online"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Cars -> {"out", "atGate", "ready", "online"}]
    /\ gate \in Cars \cup {None}
    /\ override \in 0..MaxOverride
    /\ washed \in 0..MaxWashed

Init ==
    /\ status = [c \in Cars |-> "out"]
    /\ gate = None
    /\ override = MaxOverride
    /\ washed = 0

Approach(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "out"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "atGate"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gate, override, washed>>

\* Level one: a car takes the free coarse gate lock to pass onto the ramp.
PassGate(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "atGate"
    /\ gate = None
    /\ gate' = c
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "ready"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<override, washed>>

\* Level two: admission onto the conveyor is allowed only while it is below capacity.
\* This capacity check is the sole guard keeping the conveyor within its limit.
Admit(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "ready"
    /\ gate = c
    /\ Cardinality(Online) < Cap
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "online"]
    /\ gate' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<override, washed>>

\* Privileged admin override: an admin waves a car straight on, bypassing the coarse
\* gate lock, but the conveyor capacity limit is still enforced.
AdminAdmit(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "atGate"
    /\ override > 0
    /\ Cardinality(Online) < Cap
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "online"]
    /\ override' = override - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gate, washed>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ status[c] = "online"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "out"]
    /\ washed' = IF washed < MaxWashed THEN washed + 1 ELSE washed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gate, override>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Approach(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : PassGate(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Admit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : AdminAdmit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Exit(c)

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: the number of cars on the conveyor never rises
\* above the fixed capacity, whether admitted through the gate or waved on by an admin.
WithinCapacity ==
    Cardinality(Online) <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3, c4}
    Cap = 2
    MaxOverride = 2
    MaxWashed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars through hierarchical locks taken coarse-first then
fine, and must never exceed its fixed conveyor capacity. A car first approaches the
entry gate. To pass onto the ramp it takes the free coarse entry-gate lock, which lets
one car pass the gate at a time, and becomes ready. It is then admitted onto the
conveyor only if the conveyor is currently below capacity; this capacity check is the
sole guard that keeps the number of cars on the conveyor within its limit, and on
admission the car releases the coarse gate lock. A privileged admin override lets an
admin wave a waiting car straight onto the conveyor, bypassing the coarse gate lock, but
the capacity limit is still enforced on the override path. A finished car exits the
conveyor, freeing space.

The action set is: Approach (a car arrives at the entry gate), PassGate (a car takes the
free coarse gate lock and becomes ready), Admit (a ready car is admitted onto the
conveyor only if it is below capacity, releasing the gate lock), AdminAdmit (an admin
waves a waiting car on, bypassing the gate lock but still within capacity), and Exit (a
finished car leaves the conveyor).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of cars on the conveyor never
exceeds the fixed conveyor capacity, whether they were admitted through the gate or
waved on by a privileged admin override.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m9p0t5 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES
    epoch,     \* current interlock configuration epoch
    holder,    \* the train holding the interlock critical resource, or None
    inCS,      \* inCS[t]: TRUE while train t is inside the interlock
    armed,     \* armed[t]: TRUE once t has been armed for entry (decoupled from holder)
    armEpoch   \* armEpoch[t]: the epoch at which train t was armed

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ holder \in Trains \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ armed \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ armEpoch \in [Trains -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ holder = None
    /\ inCS = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]
    /\ armed = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]
    /\ armEpoch = [t \in Trains |-> 0]

\* Arming records the current epoch; it does not consult the interlock, so several
\* trains can be armed at once.
Arm(t) ==
    /\ ~armed[t]
    /\ ~inCS[t]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ armEpoch' = [armEpoch EXCEPT ![t] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, inCS>>

\* Entry requires the interlock be free; this is the sole guard enforcing mutual
\* exclusion. The epoch match additionally blocks a train armed under an old config.
Enter(t) ==
    /\ armed[t]
    /\ armEpoch[t] = epoch
    /\ holder = None
    /\ holder' = t
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, armEpoch>>

\* Privileged admin override: an admin may admit an armed train regardless of its
\* config epoch, but the interlock-free requirement (mutual exclusion) still holds.
AdminEnter(t) ==
    /\ armed[t]
    /\ holder = None
    /\ holder' = t
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, armEpoch>>

Leave(t) ==
    /\ inCS[t]
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, armed, armEpoch>>

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch while the interlock is free.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ holder = None
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inCS, armed, armEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Arm(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Enter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : AdminEnter(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Leave(t)
    \/ Reconfigure

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any train inside the interlock must be
\* the single train recorded as its holder, so two trains never occupy the interlock
\* at once, whether admitted normally or by admin override.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A t \in Trains : inCS[t] => holder = t

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {t1, t2, t3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A subway signalling block system guards a single interlock critical resource that only
one train may occupy at a time, coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The
system keeps a current configuration epoch. A train preparing to enter is first armed,
which records the epoch in effect at that moment; arming does not consult the interlock,
so several trains can be armed at the same time. A train enters the interlock only when
the interlock is currently free, and that free-interlock requirement is the sole
mechanism enforcing exclusive occupancy; additionally, a normally admitted train must
have been armed under the current epoch, which blocks a train armed under an old
configuration. Reconfiguration advances the epoch while the interlock is free. A
privileged admin override lets an admin admit an armed train regardless of the epoch it
was armed under, but even the override honors the free-interlock requirement, so
exclusivity is preserved. A train inside eventually leaves, freeing the interlock.

The action set is: Arm (a train is armed for entry, recording the current epoch, without
checking the interlock), Enter (an armed train enters only if the interlock is free and
its epoch is current), AdminEnter (an admin admits an armed train ignoring its epoch but
still only if the interlock is free), Leave (an occupying train frees the interlock), and
Reconfigure (advance the epoch while the interlock is free).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any train inside the interlock must be the
single train recorded as its holder, so two trains never occupy the interlock at the same
time, whether admitted normally or by a privileged admin override.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m6p3t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Elevators, MaxLease

VARIABLES
    owner,     \* the elevator the dispatch slot is currently leased to, or None
    assigned,  \* assigned[e]: TRUE while elevator e believes it holds the slot
    reqs,      \* set of in-flight lease requests (elevator ids); the network reorders
    lease      \* remaining lease time on the current allocation

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Elevators \cup {None}
    /\ assigned \in [Elevators -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reqs \subseteq Elevators
    /\ lease \in 0..MaxLease

Init ==
    /\ owner = None
    /\ assigned = [e \in Elevators |-> FALSE]
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ lease = 0

\* An elevator optimistically requests the slot; requests sit in a set the dispatch
\* network may deliver in any order.
Request(e) ==
    /\ ~assigned[e]
    /\ e \notin reqs
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, assigned, lease>>

\* A lease is granted only if the slot is currently free. This free-slot guard is the
\* sole mechanism preventing the same slot being allocated to two elevators.
Grant(e) ==
    /\ e \in reqs
    /\ owner = None
    /\ owner' = e
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![e] = TRUE]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {e}
    /\ lease' = MaxLease

\* The request found the slot already leased; drop it and retry later.
Retry(e) ==
    /\ e \in reqs
    /\ owner # None
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, assigned, lease>>

\* The lease counts down over time.
Tick ==
    /\ owner # None
    /\ lease > 0
    /\ lease' = lease - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, assigned, reqs>>

\* When the lease reaches zero it expires and the slot is freed.
Expire ==
    /\ owner # None
    /\ lease = 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![owner] = FALSE]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs, lease>>

\* An elevator may finish and release the slot before the lease expires.
Release(e) ==
    /\ assigned[e]
    /\ owner = e
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![e] = FALSE]
    /\ owner' = None
    /\ lease' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Request(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Grant(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Retry(e)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Expire
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Release(e)

\* No double allocation of the same slot: any elevator that believes it holds the
\* dispatch slot must be the single elevator recorded as its owner, so the slot is
\* never leased to two elevators at once.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A e \in Elevators : assigned[e] => owner = e

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Elevators = {e1, e2, e3}
    MaxLease = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns a single shared dispatch slot to at most one
elevator car at a time using lease-based ownership with expiry. An elevator that wants
the slot optimistically submits a lease request; requests accumulate in a pool that the
dispatch network may deliver in any order. A lease is granted to an elevator only if the
slot is currently free, and this free-slot check is the only mechanism keeping the slot
from being allocated to two elevators; on grant the elevator is recorded as the slot's
owner, believes it holds the slot, and the lease timer is set. If a request finds the
slot already leased, it is dropped and the elevator retries later. The lease counts down
over time, and when it reaches zero it expires and the slot is freed; an elevator may
also finish and release the slot before the lease expires.

The action set is: Request (an elevator adds a lease request to the reorderable pool),
Grant (a lease is granted only if the slot is free, recording the owner), Retry (a
request that finds the slot leased is dropped for retry), Tick (the lease counts down),
Expire (a lease that reaches zero expires and frees the slot), and Release (the owner
finishes and frees the slot early).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any elevator that believes it holds the
dispatch slot must be the single elevator recorded as the slot's owner, so the same
dispatch slot is never double-allocated to two elevators at once.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m3p6t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxTerm, MaxServed

VARIABLES
    leader,   \* the currently elected lead controller, or None
    term,     \* the current election term
    acting,   \* acting[c]: TRUE while c is performing a protected runway allocation
    served    \* count of completed allocations (bounded activity counter)

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ acting \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ served \in 0..MaxServed

Init ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ term = 0
    /\ acting = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
    /\ served = 0

\* Elect a leader when none is in charge; the term advances.
Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, served>>

\* Failover: a new leader takes over from a slow but not failed incumbent that is not
\* mid-allocation. The old leader is no longer the leader and becomes stale.
Failover(c, d) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ c # d
    /\ ~acting[c]
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, served>>

\* An idle leader may step down, leaving no leader.
StepDown(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ ~acting[c]
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, acting, served>>

\* A protected runway allocation may be started only by the current leader; this
\* leadership check is the sole guard against a stale controller acting.
Act(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ ~acting[c]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, served>>

Finish(c) ==
    /\ acting[c]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ served' = IF served < MaxServed THEN served + 1 ELSE served
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Elect(c)
    \/ \E c, d \in Controllers : Failover(c, d)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : StepDown(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Act(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Finish(c)

\* No action by an unauthorized or stale participant: any controller performing a
\* runway allocation must be the current elected leader, so a controller superseded by
\* failover can never perform an allocation.
NoStaleAction ==
    \A c \in Controllers : acting[c] => leader = c

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxServed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator elects a single lead controller, with failover, to
perform protected runway allocations. Only the current elected leader may carry out an
allocation. When no controller is in charge, one is elected as leader and the election
term advances. A new leader may fail over from a slow but not failed incumbent that is
not currently mid-allocation; once this happens the old leader is no longer the leader
and is considered stale. Because controllers are slow but never fail, a failover is only
permitted while the incumbent is not in the middle of an allocation, so a slow leader
finishing an allocation is never cut off. An idle leader may also step down, leaving no
leader. A protected runway allocation may be started only by the controller that is the
current leader, and this leadership check is the sole guard that stops a stale
controller, one superseded by failover, from performing an allocation.

The action set is: Elect (elect a leader when none is in charge, advancing the term),
Failover (a new leader takes over from a slow, non-acting incumbent, advancing the term),
StepDown (an idle leader steps down), Act (only the current leader begins a protected
allocation), and Finish (an acting controller completes its allocation).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any controller performing a runway allocation
must be the current elected leader, so a controller that has been superseded by failover
can never perform an allocation.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od19m6p1t2 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, MaxVal, MaxLease

VARIABLES
    record,      \* the shared reservation-count record both instances update
    applied,     \* count of update commits performed
    leaseHolder, \* the instance currently holding the write lease, or None
    basis,       \* basis[i]: the record value instance i read as its update basis
    lease        \* remaining time on the current write lease

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ applied \in 0..(2 * MaxVal)
    /\ leaseHolder \in Instances \cup {None}
    /\ basis \in [Instances -> 0..MaxVal]
    /\ lease \in 0..MaxLease

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ leaseHolder = None
    /\ basis = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ lease = 0

\* Acquire the shared write lease when it is free.
AcquireLease(i) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = None
    /\ leaseHolder' = i
    /\ lease' = MaxLease
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis>>

\* The lease holder reads the current record as the basis for its update.
Read(i) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = i
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![i] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, leaseHolder, lease>>

\* A commit writes basis+1, but only if the basis still matches the record (nothing
\* was written since the read). This freshness check is the sole guard against a
\* stale-lease write clobbering updates the other instance made in between.
Commit(i) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = i
    /\ basis[i] = record
    /\ record < MaxVal
    /\ record' = basis[i] + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, basis, lease>>

\* The lease counts down and expires; a held basis is not cleared on expiry, so it
\* may become stale before the instance re-acquires the lease and commits.
Tick ==
    /\ leaseHolder # None
    /\ lease > 0
    /\ lease' = lease - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, leaseHolder, basis>>

Expire ==
    /\ leaseHolder # None
    /\ lease = 0
    /\ leaseHolder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, lease>>

ReleaseLease(i) ==
    /\ leaseHolder = i
    /\ leaseHolder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : AcquireLease(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Read(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Expire
    \/ \E i \in Instances : ReleaseLease(i)

\* No lost updates: the number of commits performed equals the shared record value, so
\* no committed update is ever lost by a stale-lease write computed from an old read.
NoLostUpdates ==
    record = applied

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    MaxVal = 3
    MaxLease = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
A library book reservation system runs two independent branch instances that share one
pool by updating a single shared reservation-count record. The right to write the record
is granted by lease-based ownership with expiry. An instance acquires the shared write
lease when it is free, reads the current record as the basis for its update, and commits
a new count equal to that basis plus one. A commit is allowed only if the record still
equals the value the instance read, meaning the other instance has not committed in
between; this freshness check is the sole guard that stops an instance from writing a
count computed from a stale read and thereby losing updates the other instance made.
The lease counts down and eventually expires, and a basis read earlier is not cleared on
expiry, so it can go stale before the instance re-acquires the lease and tries to commit.
An instance may also release the lease early.

The action set is: AcquireLease (take the free shared write lease), Read (the lease
holder reads the record as its update basis), Commit (write basis-plus-one, only if the
record is unchanged since the read), Tick (the lease counts down), Expire (a lease that
reaches zero expires and frees itself), and ReleaseLease (the holder releases the lease
early).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of update commits performed equals
the shared reservation-count record, so no committed update is ever lost by being
overwritten with a count computed from a stale read.
