------------------------------ MODULE W4Od12m2p3t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Txns, Nodes

VARIABLES
    phase,      \* phase[t]: "idle" | "preparing" | "committed" for each transaction
    vote,       \* vote[n]: the transaction node n has prepared for, or None
    prepReqs,   \* set of in-flight prepare requests [txn, node]; the network reorders
    slotOwner,  \* the transaction the contested blood-unit slot is committed to, or None
    allocated   \* allocated[t]: TRUE while transaction t believes it holds the slot

None == "none"

ClearT(t) == [n \in Nodes |-> IF vote[n] = t THEN None ELSE vote[n]]

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> {"idle", "preparing", "committed"}]
    /\ vote \in [Nodes -> Txns \cup {None}]
    /\ prepReqs \subseteq [txn : Txns, node : Nodes]
    /\ slotOwner \in Txns \cup {None}
    /\ allocated \in [Txns -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ vote = [n \in Nodes |-> None]
    /\ prepReqs = {}
    /\ slotOwner = None
    /\ allocated = [t \in Txns |-> FALSE]

\* Phase one begins: the transaction broadcasts prepare requests to every node.
Prepare(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "preparing"]
    /\ prepReqs' = prepReqs \cup {[txn |-> t, node |-> n] : n \in Nodes}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, slotOwner, allocated>>

\* A node prepares for a transaction, but only if it has not already prepared for any
\* transaction. This single-vote rule is the sole guard that keeps two transactions
\* from both gathering a unanimous prepare for the same slot.
Vote(t, n) ==
    /\ [txn |-> t, node |-> n] \in prepReqs
    /\ vote[n] = None
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![n] = t]
    /\ prepReqs' = prepReqs \ {[txn |-> t, node |-> n]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, slotOwner, allocated>>

\* Phase two: with every node prepared for it, the transaction commits the slot. There
\* is no separate lock on the slot; exclusivity rests entirely on unanimous prepares
\* being impossible for two transactions at once.
Commit(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "preparing"
    /\ \A n \in Nodes : vote[n] = t
    /\ slotOwner' = t
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, prepReqs>>

\* A preparing transaction may abort, releasing the nodes it had prepared and any of
\* its outstanding prepare requests.
Abort(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "preparing"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ vote' = ClearT(t)
    /\ prepReqs' = {r \in prepReqs : r.txn # t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, allocated>>

Release(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "committed"
    /\ slotOwner' = None
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ vote' = ClearT(t)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepReqs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Prepare(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns, n \in Nodes : Vote(t, n)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Abort(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Release(t)

\* No double allocation of the same slot: any transaction that believes it holds the
\* blood-unit slot must be the single transaction the tracker records as its owner, so
\* the same slot is never committed to two transactions at once.
NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A t \in Txns : allocated[t] => slotOwner = t

=============================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates a contested blood-unit slot to at most one
transaction using two-phase commit across its participant nodes. In phase one a
transaction broadcasts prepare requests to every node; these requests travel over a
network that can reorder them. A node prepares for a transaction only if it has not
already prepared for any transaction this round, and this single-prepare rule is the
only thing that keeps two transactions from both gathering a unanimous prepare for the
same slot. In phase two, once every node has prepared for it, the transaction commits
the slot and records itself as the slot's owner; there is no separate lock on the slot,
so correctness rests entirely on two transactions being unable to both obtain unanimous
prepares. A preparing transaction may abort, releasing the nodes it had prepared and
its outstanding prepare requests, and a committed transaction may later release the
slot.

The action set is: Prepare (a transaction broadcasts prepare requests to all nodes),
Vote (a node prepares for a transaction only if it has not prepared for any this round),
Commit (a transaction with every node prepared commits the slot and becomes owner),
Abort (a preparing transaction gives up, freeing its prepared nodes and requests), and
Release (a committed transaction frees the slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any transaction that believes it holds the
blood-unit slot must be the single transaction recorded as the slot's owner, so the same
slot is never double-allocated to two transactions at once.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od16m6p4t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requests, Cap, MaxLease, MaxDispensed

VARIABLES
    active,     \* set of requests currently holding a dispense lease (occupying capacity)
    pool,       \* set of in-flight lease-acquisition requests; the network reorders them
    leaseTime,  \* leaseTime[r]: remaining lease time for an active request r
    dispensed   \* count of completed dispenses (bounded activity counter)

TypeOK ==
    /\ active \subseteq Requests
    /\ pool \subseteq Requests
    /\ leaseTime \in [Requests -> 0..MaxLease]
    /\ dispensed \in 0..MaxDispensed

Init ==
    /\ active = {}
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ leaseTime = [r \in Requests |-> 0]
    /\ dispensed = 0

\* A dispense request asks for a lease; requests accumulate in a pool delivered in any
\* order.
Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin active
    /\ r \notin pool
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, leaseTime, dispensed>>

\* A lease is granted only while the number of active dispenses is below capacity. This
\* capacity check is the sole guard keeping concurrent dispenses within the limit.
Grant(r) ==
    /\ r \in pool
    /\ Cardinality(active) < Cap
    /\ active' = active \cup {r}
    /\ pool' = pool \ {r}
    /\ leaseTime' = [leaseTime EXCEPT ![r] = MaxLease]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed>>

\* No capacity available; the request is dropped and may be resubmitted later.
Reject(r) ==
    /\ r \in pool
    /\ Cardinality(active) >= Cap
    /\ pool' = pool \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, leaseTime, dispensed>>

\* An active lease counts down.
Tick(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ leaseTime[r] > 0
    /\ leaseTime' = [leaseTime EXCEPT ![r] = leaseTime[r] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, pool, dispensed>>

\* When its lease expires the dispense completes and frees its capacity.
Expire(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ leaseTime[r] = 0
    /\ active' = active \ {r}
    /\ dispensed' = IF dispensed < MaxDispensed THEN dispensed + 1 ELSE dispensed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leaseTime>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Submit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Grant(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Reject(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Tick(r)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Expire(r)

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: the number of concurrently active dispense
\* leases never rises above the fixed capacity, however requests are reordered.
WithinCapacity ==
    Cardinality(active) <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Requests = {q1, q2, q3, q4}
    Cap = 2
    MaxLease = 2
    MaxDispensed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser limits how many dispenses run concurrently, never
exceeding a fixed capacity, and grants each active dispense a lease that expires. A
dispense request asks for a lease; requests accumulate in a pool that the network may
deliver in any order. A lease is granted to a request only while the number of active
dispenses is below capacity, and this capacity check is the sole mechanism keeping the
number of concurrent dispenses within the limit; on grant the request becomes active
and its lease timer is set. If no capacity is available, the request is dropped and may
be resubmitted later. An active lease counts down over time, and when it expires the
dispense completes and frees its capacity for another request.

The action set is: Submit (a request joins the reorderable pool asking for a lease),
Grant (a lease is granted only while below capacity, making the request active), Reject
(a request is dropped when no capacity is available), Tick (an active lease counts down),
and Expire (an expired lease completes the dispense and frees its capacity).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of concurrently active dispense
leases never exceeds the fixed capacity, no matter how lease requests are reordered.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m1p1t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Elevators, MaxVal

VARIABLES
    record,    \* the shared load-tally record all cars update
    applied,   \* count of update commits performed
    token,     \* the ring token holder (only holder may touch the record), or None
    basis,     \* basis[e]: the record value car e last read as its update basis
    capacity   \* the load capacity limit, which may change at runtime

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ applied \in 0..(2 * MaxVal)
    /\ token \in Elevators \cup {None}
    /\ basis \in [Elevators -> 0..MaxVal]
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxVal

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ token = None
    /\ basis = [e \in Elevators |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = MaxVal

\* The ring hands the free token to a car.
Acquire(e) ==
    /\ token = None
    /\ token' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, capacity>>

Release(e) ==
    /\ token = e
    /\ token' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, basis, capacity>>

\* The token holder reads the record as its update basis.
Read(e) ==
    /\ token = e
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![e] = record]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, token, capacity>>

\* A commit writes basis+1, but only if the basis is still current and the record is
\* below the current capacity. The freshness check is the sole guard against a stale
\* write, carried over from a previous token round, clobbering intervening updates.
Commit(e) ==
    /\ token = e
    /\ basis[e] = record
    /\ record < capacity
    /\ record' = basis[e] + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, basis, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime.
SetCapacity(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, token, basis>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Acquire(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Release(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Read(e)
    \/ \E e \in Elevators : Commit(e)
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxVal : SetCapacity(c)

\* No lost updates: the number of update commits performed equals the shared record, so
\* no committed update is ever lost by a stale write carried over across token rounds.
NoLostUpdates ==
    record = applied

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Elevators = {e1, e2, e3}
    MaxVal = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has several cars that all update a single shared
load-tally record. Exclusive access to the record is granted by a token ring: a
circulating token is held by at most one car at a time, and only the token holder may
read or update the record. To make an update, the holder first reads the current record
as its basis, then commits a new value equal to that basis plus one. A commit is allowed
only if the basis is still current, that is, the record has not changed since the read,
and only while the record is below the current capacity limit; the freshness check is
what stops a car from writing a value computed from a stale read, one carried over from
a previous token round, and thereby clobbering updates made in between. The load capacity
limit may change at runtime.

The action set is: Acquire (a car takes the free token), Release (the holder returns the
token to the ring), Read (the holder reads the record as its update basis), Commit (the
holder writes basis-plus-one, only if the basis is current and the record is below
capacity), and SetCapacity (change the capacity limit at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of update commits performed equals
the shared load-tally record, so no committed update is ever lost by being overwritten
with a value computed from a stale read.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od19m7p4t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Patrons, Cap, MaxCount, MaxOverride

VARIABLES
    count,     \* the shared reservation-count register (bounded by capacity Cap)
    rbasis,    \* rbasis[p]: the count value patron p read for its compare-and-swap
    reading,   \* reading[p]: TRUE while patron p has an outstanding CAS attempt
    override   \* remaining privileged admin overrides

TypeOK ==
    /\ count \in 0..MaxCount
    /\ rbasis \in [Patrons -> 0..MaxCount]
    /\ reading \in [Patrons -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ override \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
    /\ count = 0
    /\ rbasis = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
    /\ reading = [p \in Patrons |-> FALSE]
    /\ override = MaxOverride

\* A patron reads the current count as the basis for its compare-and-swap.
Read(p) ==
    /\ ~reading[p]
    /\ rbasis' = [rbasis EXCEPT ![p] = count]
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, override>>

\* Compare-and-swap increment: succeeds only if the count is unchanged since the read
\* and is still below capacity. The capacity guard is the sole check keeping the count
\* within its limit.
CASIncr(p) ==
    /\ reading[p]
    /\ rbasis[p] = count
    /\ count < Cap
    /\ count' = count + 1
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rbasis, override>>

\* The compare failed (count moved since the read); drop and retry.
CASFail(p) ==
    /\ reading[p]
    /\ rbasis[p] # count
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, rbasis, override>>

\* A reservation is released, freeing one unit of capacity.
Decr(p) ==
    /\ count > 0
    /\ count' = count - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rbasis, reading, override>>

\* Privileged admin override: an admin reserves directly, bypassing the CAS protocol,
\* but the capacity limit is still enforced.
AdminReserve ==
    /\ override > 0
    /\ count < Cap
    /\ count' = count + 1
    /\ override' = override - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rbasis, reading>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Read(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : CASIncr(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : CASFail(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Decr(p)
    \/ AdminReserve

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: the shared reservation count never rises above
\* the fixed capacity, whether incremented via compare-and-swap or by an admin override.
WithinCapacity ==
    count <= Cap

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Patrons = {p1, p2, p3}
    Cap = 2
    MaxCount = 4
    MaxOverride = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A library book reservation system caps how many active reservations a popular title may
have, never exceeding a fixed capacity, and updates a shared reservation-count register
using a compare-and-swap. A patron reserving first reads the current count as the basis
for its compare-and-swap. It then attempts a compare-and-swap increment, which succeeds
only if the count is unchanged since the read and is still below capacity; the capacity
guard is the sole check that keeps the count within its limit. If the compare fails
because the count moved, the patron drops its attempt and retries. A reservation may be
released, freeing one unit of capacity. A privileged admin override lets an admin reserve
directly, bypassing the compare-and-swap protocol, but the capacity limit is still
enforced on the override path.

The action set is: Read (a patron reads the count as its compare-and-swap basis), CASIncr
(a compare-and-swap increment succeeds only if the count is unchanged and below capacity),
CASFail (a patron whose compare fails drops its attempt to retry), Decr (a reservation is
released, freeing capacity), and AdminReserve (an admin reserves directly, bypassing the
compare-and-swap but still within capacity).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the shared reservation count never exceeds the
fixed capacity, whether it was incremented via compare-and-swap or by a privileged admin
override.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od12m1p0t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxPass

VARIABLES
    token,    \* the ring token holder, or None if the token is momentarily lost
    inCS,     \* inCS[p]: TRUE while node p is inside the shared-ledger critical section
    crashed,  \* crashed[p]: TRUE if node p has silently crashed
    passes    \* count of token passes (bounded activity counter)

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Nodes \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ crashed \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ passes \in 0..MaxPass

Init ==
    /\ token = None
    /\ inCS = [p \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ crashed = [p \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ passes = 0

\* The ring regenerates a lost token onto an alive node.
Regen(q) ==
    /\ token = None
    /\ ~crashed[q]
    /\ token' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, crashed, passes>>

\* The holder passes the token along the ring to another alive node when not in its
\* critical section.
PassToken(p, q) ==
    /\ token = p
    /\ p # q
    /\ ~inCS[p]
    /\ ~crashed[q]
    /\ token' = q
    /\ passes' = IF passes < MaxPass THEN passes + 1 ELSE passes
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, crashed>>

\* Entry to the critical section requires holding the token; this token check is the
\* sole guard enforcing mutual exclusion of the shared ledger.
EnterCS(p) ==
    /\ token = p
    /\ ~inCS[p]
    /\ ~crashed[p]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, passes>>

ExitCS(p) ==
    /\ inCS[p]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, passes>>

\* A node may crash silently while not in its critical section, and never the last
\* alive one; if it held the token, the token is lost until regenerated.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ ~crashed[p]
    /\ ~inCS[p]
    /\ \E o \in Nodes : o # p /\ ~crashed[o]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ token' = IF token = p THEN None ELSE token
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, passes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E q \in Nodes : Regen(q)
    \/ \E p, q \in Nodes : PassToken(p, q)
    \/ \E p \in Nodes : EnterCS(p)
    \/ \E p \in Nodes : ExitCS(p)
    \/ \E p \in Nodes : Crash(p)

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any node inside the shared-ledger critical
\* section must be the current token holder, so two nodes never enter it at once, even as
\* nodes crash silently and the token is regenerated.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A p \in Nodes : inCS[p] => token = p

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {b1, b2, b3}
    MaxPass = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker replicates a shared ledger across several nodes, and only
one node may enter the ledger critical section at a time. Exclusive access is granted by
a token ring: a single circulating token is held by at most one node, and the ring
regenerates a lost token onto an alive node. The token holder passes the token along the
ring to another alive node when it is not in its critical section. A node enters the
critical section only while it holds the token, and this token check is the sole
mechanism enforcing exclusive access to the ledger. A node inside the section eventually
exits. Any node except the last alive one may crash silently while not in its critical
section; if a crashing node held the token, the token is lost until the ring regenerates
it.

The action set is: Regen (the ring places a lost token onto an alive node), PassToken
(the holder passes the token to another alive node while not in its critical section),
EnterCS (a node enters the critical section only while holding the token), ExitCS (a node
leaves the critical section), and Crash (a node other than the last alive one crashes
silently while not in its section, dropping the token if it held it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any node inside the ledger critical section
must be the current token holder, so two nodes never occupy the critical section at the
same time.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m8p6t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxCap

VARIABLES
    coarse,    \* holder of the coarse sector lock, or None
    fine,      \* holder of the fine runway lock (taken only after coarse), or None
    acting,    \* acting[c]: TRUE while controller c is performing a runway allocation
    capacity   \* number of open sectors, which changes at runtime

None == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ fine \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ acting \in [Controllers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ fine = None
    /\ acting = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* Level one: take the free coarse sector lock, allowed only while a sector is open.
GrabCoarse(c) ==
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ capacity > 0
    /\ coarse' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, acting, capacity>>

\* Level two: take the fine runway lock while holding the coarse lock.
GrabFine(c) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ fine = None
    /\ fine' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, acting, capacity>>

\* The protected runway allocation may be started only while the controller holds the
\* fine runway lock; this authorization check is the sole guard against a stale
\* controller, one whose lock has been revoked, acting.
Act(c) ==
    /\ fine = c
    /\ ~acting[c]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, capacity>>

Finish(c) ==
    /\ acting[c]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, capacity>>

\* A controller not mid-allocation may be revoked, releasing both its locks; if it held
\* the fine lock it becomes stale.
Revoke(c) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ ~acting[c]
    /\ coarse' = None
    /\ fine' = IF fine = c THEN None ELSE fine
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acting, capacity>>

\* The number of open sectors changes at runtime.
SetCapacity(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, acting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GrabCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GrabFine(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Act(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Finish(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Revoke(c)
    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxCap : SetCapacity(k)

\* No action by an unauthorized or stale participant: any controller performing a runway
\* allocation must currently hold the fine runway lock, so a controller whose lock has
\* been revoked can never perform an allocation.
NoStaleAction ==
    \A c \in Controllers : acting[c] => fine = c

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator authorizes protected runway allocations through
hierarchical locks taken coarse-first then fine. A controller must first take the free
coarse sector lock, which is allowed only while a sector is open, and only then may it
take the fine runway lock. A protected runway allocation may be started only while the
controller holds the fine runway lock, and this authorization check is the sole guard
that stops a stale controller, one whose lock has been revoked, from performing an
allocation. A controller that is not currently mid-allocation may be revoked, releasing
both of its locks; if it held the fine lock it becomes stale. The number of open sectors
changes at runtime, which governs when the coarse sector lock may be taken.

The action set is: GrabCoarse (take the free coarse sector lock while a sector is open),
GrabFine (take the fine runway lock while holding the coarse lock), Act (begin a
protected allocation only while holding the fine runway lock), Finish (complete an
allocation), Revoke (release both locks of a controller not mid-allocation, leaving it
stale if it held the fine lock), and SetCapacity (change the number of open sectors at
runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, any controller performing a runway allocation
must currently hold the fine runway lock, so a controller whose lock has been revoked can
never perform an allocation.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m1p2t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Belts, Movers, Total, MaxCap

VARIABLES
    bags,      \* bags[belt]: number of bags currently resting on belt
    transit,   \* number of bags picked up by the token holder and in transit
    token,     \* the ring token holder (only holder may move bags), or None
    capacity   \* per-belt capacity, which may change at runtime

None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumF(_)
SumF(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN bags[x] + SumF(S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ bags \in [Belts -> 0..Total]
    /\ transit \in 0..Total
    /\ token \in Movers \cup {None}
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ bags = [b \in Belts |-> IF b = CHOOSE z \in Belts : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ token = None
    /\ capacity = MaxCap

\* The ring hands the free token to a mover.
Acquire(m) ==
    /\ token = None
    /\ token' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit, capacity>>

\* Releasing returns the token, but only when not carrying a bag.
Release(m) ==
    /\ token = m
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ token' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit, capacity>>

\* The token holder lifts one bag off a belt into transit.
Pickup(m, belt) ==
    /\ token = m
    /\ bags[belt] > 0
    /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![belt] = bags[belt] - 1]
    /\ transit' = transit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, capacity>>

\* The token holder sets an in-transit bag down onto a belt with room.
Putdown(m, belt) ==
    /\ token = m
    /\ transit > 0
    /\ bags[belt] < capacity
    /\ transit' = transit - 1
    /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![belt] = bags[belt] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, capacity>>

\* Per-belt capacity changes at runtime.
SetCapacity(k) ==
    /\ k # capacity
    /\ capacity' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit, token>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Movers : Acquire(m)
    \/ \E m \in Movers : Release(m)
    \/ \E m \in Movers, belt \in Belts : Pickup(m, belt)
    \/ \E m \in Movers, belt \in Belts : Putdown(m, belt)
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxCap : SetCapacity(k)

\* Conservation of a quantity: the bags resting on belts plus those in transit always
\* sum to the fixed total, so the router never creates or loses a bag, even as belt
\* capacity changes at runtime.
Conservation ==
    SumF(Belts) + transit = Total

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Belts = {g1, g2, g3}
    Movers = {m1, m2}
    Total = 2
    MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
An airport baggage router moves a fixed number of bags among its belts, and the total
number of bags in the whole system never changes. Exclusive permission to move bags is
granted by a token ring: a single circulating token is held by at most one mover at a
time, and only the token holder may move bags. The holder lifts one bag off a belt into
transit, and later sets an in-transit bag down onto a belt that has room under its
current capacity. A mover may release the token only when it is not carrying a bag. Each
bag is therefore always either resting on exactly one belt or in transit, and the router
never creates a new bag or loses one. The per-belt capacity may change at runtime, which
governs when a bag may be set down on a belt.

The action set is: Acquire (a mover takes the free token), Release (a mover returns the
token, only when not carrying a bag), Pickup (the token holder lifts one bag off a belt
into transit), Putdown (the token holder sets an in-transit bag onto a belt with room),
and SetCapacity (change the per-belt capacity at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the bags resting on belts plus those in transit
sum to exactly the fixed total, so the router never creates or loses a bag.
